title.narrative: GLA 2 - Indonesia

description.narrative: We envision that the forest in Indonesia is maintained at the current extent and cover, and that it contributesto Indonesia’s commitments on climate change mitigation and adaptation. Government and private sector, including financiers, commit to zero- deforestation and sustainability principles, whereas IPLCs who dwell in forested landscapes sustainably govern and responsibly manage forest areas, sustain local livelihoods and are resilient to climate change impacts. In a broader scope, citizens, including (W)EHRDs, are rights literate, enjoy human and women’s rights, and safely participate in a social movement within a democratic manner. GLA2 Indonesia aims to contribute to that vision, and to do so we set up the following goals for the country programme. By 2025, we aim that:1. IPLCs in the four landscapes have sovereign control over their lands and natural resources, and conductecologically and socially responsible livelihoods.2. Government and private sector operating in the four landscapes formalise the halting of new licences in forest and peatlands and rightfully implement environmental and social standards for the existingplantations/concessions, including respect to labour and human rights. At the same time, Indonesianbanks apply sustainable financial principles and standards to their investment for agro-commodity andextractive industries.3. (W)EHRDs in Indonesia freely express their opinions, safely participate in public affairs, and are rightfully protected by the laws while the National Commission on Human Rights provides support through the (W)EHRDs special task force and policy instrument.

CSOs succeeded in creating space for CSO demandsand positions through agenda setting, influencing the debateand/or creating space to engage at national and international level 5 times. For example: The Tampo Lore Festival was covered by Nusantaratv which contributed to the preservation and protection of the traditional cultural values of Tampo Lore, as well as community livelihood resources and support to sustainable development from involved parties.

No 1st ring youth led CSO partners are expected to increase their capacity over the course of the GLA2 programme in Cameroon. No 2nd ring youth led CSO partners have been included in this target value, as the GLA is a flexible adaptable program this can't be well estimated in advance.

1 private sector company policy for sustainable and inclusive development was better implemented as a result of CSO engagement at midline. The Padang branch of M-Block Market, owned by PT Ruang Market Millenial, is a modern grocery market with the spirit of being a place for selling local products and selling 70% local brands. After passing the curation process, the agarwood leaf tea herbal drink brand is considered to meet the standards and can be marketed at M-Block Market outlets.
